name: Stoneware Baked Spaghetti with Ground Beef & Hidden Vegetables
sub: Hearty baked protein spaghetti with ground beef, finely chopped vegetables, and Four Cheese pasta sauce
text:
INGREDIENTS
12 oz Al Dente Protein Spaghetti
1 lb 80/20 ground beef
1 medium onion, finely chopped
2-3 celery ribs, finely chopped
2-3 carrots, grated or finely chopped
1 jar (25 oz) 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce
1/2 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp dried oregano or Italian seasoning
Salt, to taste
Black pepper, to taste

OPTIONAL TOPPING
2-4 Tbsp grated Parmesan cheese or crushed pork rinds

DIRECTIONS
1. Preheat the oven to 375 F. Cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente. Drain well and set aside.
2. Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it apart as it cooks. Drain excess fat if needed.
3. Add the onion, celery, and carrots. Continue cooking until the vegetables are tender and beginning to brown. Grating the carrots and finely chopping the celery and onion helps the vegetables blend into the finished sauce.
4. Pour the entire jar of 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce into the skillet. Add the garlic powder, oregano or Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
5. Add the cooked spaghetti to the meat and vegetable sauce and toss until evenly coated. Lightly grease a large stoneware baking dish, transfer the spaghetti mixture to the dish, and spread evenly.
6. If desired, sprinkle the top with grated Parmesan cheese or crushed pork rinds. Cover with foil and bake at 375 F for 25-30 minutes, until hot throughout. Remove the foil and broil for 2-3 minutes for a lightly browned top, watching closely to prevent burning.
7. Let the baked spaghetti rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

NOTES
Slightly undercook the spaghetti during the initial boil so it does not become overly soft during baking.

This recipe uses a full 25 oz jar of 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce.

This recipe is designed for a large stoneware baking dish. A comparable large casserole dish may also be used.

Parmesan adds a cheesy finish, while crushed pork rinds add texture and crunch.

PASTA STANDARD
Unless a recipe specifically states otherwise, pasta recipes on The Well-Seasoned Life use Al Dente Protein Pasta. Nutrition information is based on the pasta and other ingredients presented in the recipe.

NUTRITION
Estimated whole casserole: approximately 2,400-2,500 calories.

Estimated calorie contribution: 1 lb 80/20 ground beef, approximately 1,150 calories; 12 oz Al Dente Protein Spaghetti, approximately 720-750 calories; 25 oz 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce, approximately 360-420 calories; onion, carrots, and celery, approximately 100 calories; optional topping, approximately 80 calories.

Nutrition estimates are based on the ingredients and quantities presented. Changes to ingredient brands, varieties, quantities, or optional toppings will affect the final calories and macros.
